1.plain: All four pots sit under the 80° valve on the numbers and none moved today: Iran 69° (6.0), US 78° (6.8), Small Gulf 69° (6.0), Saudi–UAE 77° (6.7). The Saudi fall of 03:00 — the Taif death aging out of the seven-day window — is still held for the house's tick, so the day's point is written plain. What is inside the numbers: the rial firmed to 233,600; Brent at $105.7 nudged the US door term a hair; no US force was fired on and no US military aircraft was even on the feed over the Gulf at 14:11 UTC; the Qatar channel is open and the seven-day roadmap is on the record, which keeps Iran's 'talks' term at its lowest setting. Tomorrow's arithmetic: the Sep 18 Italian-jet hit leaves the Saudi window at 03:00 and the pot reads 5.2 unless a confirmed hit lands first.
1.trade: Brent $104.1 at 18:05 UTC (-2.3% on the day, ~+0.5% on the week) is trading the phased-deal reports and Araghchi's Saudi and Egyptian meetings against the Mecca-pact chiefs in Riyadh; WTI $92.3 with the Brent–WTI spread the widest since May, so the US pump-price term will not fall with WTI. Two tenths under the valve, the US pot goes over on one US force fired on or Brent back above ~$110; it goes down on a US 'yes' to the roadmap's first step (the blockade) — Pigott's 'actions-based' is not that. The Saudi pot is the one to watch for a mechanical swing: 5.2 tomorrow on nothing, straight back over 80° on one confirmed hit. Reuters' nine transits Thursday, not the sixty, is the number for the door.

2.plain: The door closed Thursday at 12 in / 11 out with 76 hulls inside, and by 10:00 UTC Friday had two in and eight out with 51 inside. The 24-hour log has an LNG, an LPG and a products tanker out and an LPG and an oil/chemical tanker in — nothing crude-sized either way — and no new export barrel has been logged in sixteen hours. Reuters' own preliminary shiptracking counted nine transits on Thursday, down from 14: eight exits, among them one laden VLCC and a ballast gas carrier, and a single handymax bulker inbound; the ten-day average is about 18. That is the measured door. The US official's sixty ships on Wednesday still has no second source, no CENTCOM word and no AIS echo; PortWatch, stuck at Sep 20, will say.
2.trade: Each week under 10 transits/day has lifted Brent; creditor selling steepens the curve.

3.plain: Carriers hold outside Iran's 300 km ring; the fight is inside it. USNI Sep 14: both carriers and the Boxer group in the Arabian Sea, no US warship named inside the Gulf; Ross back with Bush.
3.trade: A carrier inside the ring is the tell for a wider war.

4.plain: Forty-nine items wait for the house's tick — and NOTHING new was held at Sep 25 11:00 either. The referee's reasons: Araghchi's meeting with the Saudi foreign minister (IRIB) is a Saudi–Iran contact with no rule row of its own and sits on the New York thread already held (2026-09-24 03:00-4) — a recheck, not a new row; Pigott's 'actions-based' answer has no row; the Riyadh chiefs met and Erdogan ruled out an automatic military reply — no row; the Council condemned the Houthis, not Iran, and France's text is still not tabled; nothing was hit at sea or on land in 60 hours. The '60 ships' claim (23:00-1) reached its 48-hour mark WITH a second region (the official told Al Jazeera himself), so it is not withdrawn — it stays yours, leaning reject on the measured feeds. The Saudi crossing of 03:00 (03:00-1) is still yours and still matters for tomorrow: either way the pot reads 5.2 at 03:00 unless a confirmed hit lands.
4.trade: A confirmed pipeline hit is the rung-7 print that re-prices Brent; watch for a rung-9 act (a US warship actually hit) or the first rung-10 act since February.

5.plain: Most likely next 14 days (Sep 24 freeze, window to Oct 8): Iran seizes or fires on a tanker (41%); a Gulf energy strike is the second card (30%); the Houthis on the Red Sea third (18%); a US warship hit 14%. US: sink more Iranian tankers 53%, bigger escorted convoys 39%, a pause that blesses the corridor 14%. The posteriors have not moved since Sep 11 because every signal since then is held for the house's tick — the 80-country statement, if ticked alone, would move Iran's 'Widen the war' from 1.5% to 2.6% and nothing else. Scorecard after three graded days: Iran's top call has landed three times out of three; the US top call — 'sink more tankers' — has missed twice running (nothing sunk since Sep 8). Brier 0.154.
5.trade: Tanker rates and war-risk premia up; XLE over SPX; long-dated Brent calls cheap if force-scenario odds are right.

6.plain: Iran wants to force an escalation before Nov 3; the US wants to squeeze and hold.
6.trade: No deal premium: fade rallies on 'talks' headlines unless a convoy actually transits.

7.plain: America's quiet bill, Thursday close: the ten-year at 5.11% and the thirty-year at 5.40% (Sep 23, FRED) — the highest since 2007 and 2004 — with 5.16% and 5.45% printed intraday Thursday; gas $4.478; foreign official custody of Treasuries down $11.4B on the week to $2,597.5B, the third fall in four weeks and about $145B below end-April. Iran's parliament speaker is keeping score in public ('Happy 5.1% 10Y America'). The Senate declined, 49-50, to make the war the president's problem before Nov 3 — so the bill stays his.
7.trade: Bear-steepener with official selling: a custody week of +$30B after an intervention has marked the local top in yields twice (Jul 29, Aug 26) — this week was -$11B, so no top signal. DXY firm short-term (safe haven), soft long-term (reserve share).

8.plain: Iran and the small Gulf states pay; Israel doesn't.
8.trade: Qatar and Kuwait sovereign spreads wider; Israeli equities unaffected.

9.plain: Russia and Egypt win; Asia's importers lose; creditors trim.
9.trade: Long RUB oil revenue proxies; short INR/JPY on oil-import stress.

10.plain: The engine (lobby, arms, oil) still beats the brake (voters) — but the gap is closing.
10.trade: LMT/RTX hold while engine ≥8; first brake-over-engine print is the sell signal.

11.plain: Bigger war 33%, Stuck 31%, Strait regime 17%, Signed deal 8%, Regime change 6%.
11.trade: Bigger-war above 30% is the level to hedge with long-dated Brent calls; Signed deal above 20% is the level for Brent < $85.

12.plain: Weak signals: a Saudi readout of the Araghchi–Faisal meeting (if Riyadh confirms it, the Saudi 'talks' term is live by two accounts); whether Washington answers the seven-day roadmap's first step before Rezaei's ~Sep 27–28 window closes, or 'actions-based' is the whole answer; whether Paris circulates the navigation-mission text and what Moscow and Beijing say to it; whether the Riyadh chiefs' meeting produces deployments or a communiqué after Erdogan's ceiling; whether Iran's Iraq ticket halt becomes a NOTAM or a drone near an airport; whether PortWatch's Sep 21–24 prints back Reuters' nine or the official's sixty; whether the 60-hour quiet at sea holds through the weekend or UKMTO logs #143; and the Saudi pot's 5.2 tomorrow on nothing — or 80°+ on one confirmed hit.

tiles.counter: one scale for every pot: 100° = boils over (a side gives up its aim); 80° = the emergency valve, past which a side is forced to escalate and acts against its own interest. Underneath, every pot shares one trigger on the 0–10 score — 7.0, the valve (re-fit monthly, the same for all four); the display maps 7.0 to 80° and 10 to 100°, so a degree means the same thing in every pot and the gap from 80° to 100° is a side's remaining tolerance

tiles.counter: AIS shows only ships that broadcast — dark tankers and most warships are invisible; ADS-B shows only aircraft with transponders on — military aircraft over Iran do not broadcast, so an empty sky is 'not seen', not 'not there'. Dead-reckoned positions are extrapolations, not fixes. Thermal anomalies cannot say what burned or who lit it
tiles.source: Live layer: every AIS commercial ship from hormuz.data-tracking.net /api/ships (MarineTraffic feeds, 30-min polls) and every ADS-B aircraft from adsb.lol (four 250-nm circles) — rebuilt every 10 minutes by a GitHub Action (live.json) and, between fixes, moved along last course and speed (dead reckoning, ≤20 min). Basemap: NASA VIIRS true colour via GIBS, newest complete pass (date on the toggle). Fire dots: VIIRS 375 m thermal anomalies, last 48 h (flares are normal; a new dot at a port, refinery or base is the signal). US warship positions: USNI Fleet & Marine Tracker (weekly, Monday) — the tracker names the sea, the point inside it is ours (JUDGMENT); roster as of Sep 8: George Washington + George H.W. Export-engine bars: same customs/ministry releases; Russia surplus = Jan–May monthly average; ringgit at 4.2 RM/$.
tiles.counter: These are correlations with the war window, not attributions: Korea and Malaysia are riding the AI-chip cycle, China's record exports are partly tariff front-running and a weak yuan, Brazil's crude surge started before March. Russia's beat is Q2 y/y against a weak 2025 base and its budget oil take is still falling. Most trade prints are one month; Q2 GDP is preliminary and gets revised.
tiles.moves: Monthly: China customs (~7th), Korea MOTIE (1st), Brazil MDIC (1st week), Malaysia DOSM (~20th), Russian MinFin oil & gas revenue (3rd). Quarterly: Q3 GDP prints late Oct (Korea, China) and Nov (Russia, Brazil). IMF October WEO replaces the July forecast column.
tiles.trade: The trade is not Russia or China — it is the AI-hardware exporters (Korea, Malaysia, Taiwan) and non-Gulf crude exporters (Brazil) that carry a war premium without war exposure; China gets export volume but no domestic lift; Russia gets prices and a current-account cushion but not budget cash.
